successCriteria.description: `SeedService.seed()` is idempotent: invoking it twice against the same database inserts no duplicate rows — every entity is looked up by its natural key (employee by employeeNumber/email, leave type by code, policy by leaveTypeCode+effectiveFrom, balance by employeeId+leaveTypeCode+periodStart+periodEnd, request by the composite (employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date)) and skipped when present, with no delete-and-reinsert.

The seed produces a consistent dataset: for each seeded leave request, the owning employee's current-period balance reflects the reservation arithmetic — SUBMITTED requests contribute their `requestedDays` to `pendingDays` and APPROVED requests contribute to `usedDays` — so `entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays` equals the true available days.
`src/modules/seed/index.ts` re-exports `ISeedService` and `SeedService` as the module's public entry point, and `ISeedService` declares exactly one method `seed(): Promise<void>`.
Jest unit tests under `tests/unit/modules/seed/` pass, covering idempotency (running twice inserts no duplicates) and balance/request consistency, using an in-memory or fake knex client.

constraints: Seed writes go directly through the injected knex client — no repository layer is introduced for the seed module (the architecture declares seed depends only on shared-date and shared-types, with no repository interfaces).

No hardcoded credential string: the seeded password plaintext is read from `process.env.SEED_PASSWORD` with a documented default, and `passwordHash` is minted via `bcrypt.hashSync(plaintext, 10)` — the same call the auth service verifies with.
No magic id strings: every seeded row's `id` is generated via `randomUUID()`; the seed never invents sentinel ids and never delete-and-reinserts (a hand-edited demo DB must not be destroyed).
The current accrual period for each balance is derived with `periodContaining` from `src/shared/date` anchored on each employee's `hireDate` — never a hand-written date literal.
`requestedDays` is computed via the shared `requestedDays(startDate, endDate)` helper from `src/shared/types` — never re-derived locally.

Every type is imported from the exact module path the architecture declares for it (enums + `requestedDays` from `src/shared/types`, `periodContaining` from `src/shared/date`, entity models from their respective `src/modules/<name>/<name>.model.ts`), and entity field shapes are used verbatim — no field renamed, split, added, or omitted.
outOfScope: The knex seed entry (`seeds/development_seed.js`), knexfile wiring, and the `npm run seed` script — these belong to Phase 2 and are intentionally absent.
Root `npm run dev` script, `web/package.json` test-script fix, and README documentation — Phase 3 deliverables.
Any HTTP routes, controllers, RBAC guards, audit-log writes, or notification side effects — the seed is a one-shot dev script with no API surface.

entityInvariants.invariant: The seed mints exactly two employees — one MANAGER and one EMPLOYEE whose `managerId` links the employee to the manager — both with `employmentStatus = ACTIVE`, `terminationDate = null`, and a `passwordHash` minted via `bcrypt.hashSync(SEED_PASSWORD, 10)`.
The seed inserts at minimum the `annual` leave type plus every other leave type referenced by a seeded policy, using the canonical LeaveType field shape with `code` as the natural key.
Every seeded policy has `status = LeavePolicyStatus.ACTIVE` and a `leaveTypeCode` that references a seeded leave type, so the balance logic can resolve entitlements and accrual periods.

A current-period balance is seeded for BOTH the manager and the employee, with `periodStart`/`periodEnd` derived from `periodContaining(hireDate, accrualPeriodMonths, now)` and counters consistent with the seeded requests.

Two or three requests are seeded in different lifecycle states (e.g. SUBMITTED and APPROVED, optionally DRAFT/REJECTED), each with `requestedDays` computed via the shared helper and `id` generated via `randomUUID()`; idempotency is keyed on the deterministic composite (employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Idempotent: safe to run repeatedly; skips any row whose natural key already exists rather than failing or duplicating.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the canonical `requestedDays(startDate, endDate)` inclusive day-count helper (endDate - startDate + 1) — never re-derive it locally.
Reuse `periodContaining` (and its `startOfUtcDay`/`addMonths` companions) to derive the current accrual period anchored on each employee's hireDate — never a hand-written date.

Match the Employee field shape exactly (id, employeeNumber, firstName, lastName, email, role, managerId, department, hireDate, terminationDate, employmentStatus, passwordHash) — no field renamed, split, added, or omitted.
Match the LeaveType field shape exactly (code, name, requiresApproval, maxConsecutiveDays, isPaid).

Match the LeavePolicy field shape exactly (id, leaveTypeCode, policyName, annualEntitlementDays, accrualPeriodMonths, carryForwardDays, minNoticeDays, maxRequestDays, requiresManagerApproval, effectiveFrom, effectiveTo, status) and use `LeavePolicyStatus.ACTIVE`.
Match the LeaveBalance field shape exactly (id, employeeId, leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd, entitledDays, usedDays, pendingDays).

Match the LeaveRequest field shape exactly (id, employeeId, leaveTypeCode, startDate, endDate, requestedDays, reason, status, approverId, approvalComment, submittedAt, decidedAt, cancelledBy, cancelledAt) and use `LeaveStatus` enum values.

Write to the snake_case column names the schema declares (employee_number, first_name, last_name, password_hash, manager_id, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, leave_type_code, policy_name, annual_entitlement_days, accrual_period_months, carry_forward_days, min_notice_days, max_request_days, requires_manager_approval, effective_from, effective_to, period_start, period_end, entitled_days, used_days, pending_days, start_date, end_date, requested_days, approver_id, approval_comment, submitted_at, decided_at, cancelled_by, cancelled_at).

integrationPoints.why: Canonical enums (LeaveTypeCode, EmployeeRole, EmploymentStatus, LeaveStatus) and the `requestedDays` helper the seed must reuse.
`periodContaining` (with startOfUtcDay/addMonths) to derive the current accrual period for each balance.
`bcrypt.hashSync(plaintext, 10)` to mint password hashes the auth service's `bcrypt.compare` can verify.
The seed writes directly through the injected knex instance; no repository layer is introduced for the seed module.
